newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWISS SHARES LOSE TWO PERCENT ON FUTURES' PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: SWISS SHARES LOSE TWO PERCENT ON FUTURES' PRESSURE.

text.p: 1455 GMT - Swiss shares ended near their day's lows, giving up more than two percent in a broad downward move that was largely to derivatives-linked selling.
"We saw a lot of pressure from the SMI future," one dealer said, adding today's U.S. economic data were basically favourable, but did not improve market sentiment.
The market was expected to remain volatile ahead of U.S. CPI and jobless claims on Thursday and the expiry of options and futures on Friday.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slid 126.3 points, or 2.17 percent to 5,682.1 points.
* The Swiss Performance Index (SPI) of all shares ended donwn 72.40 point, or 1.95 percent, at 3,640.95.
Bourse volume was at 3.30 billion Swiss francs.
* Shares of bank group SBC, which for a long time today were able to resist the downward drag in the market, ended off two francs at 415.

SBC's group net profit rose 84 percent in the first half year, well above analysts' forecasts of a rise of 50 to 70 percent. "SBC was the only major Swiss bank which exceeded the market's expectations," one trader said.
SBC was also seen profiting from switches from other banks.
Credit Suisse Group and Winterthur, which announced merger plans on Monday, continued to fall.

CS Group was down 13.25 franc at 190.25. Winterthur lost 88 francs to 1,416. One dealer said the sentiment for the two stocks was still poor. Analysts have expressed some reservations about the cost and timing of the merger.
Novartis registereds led the actives list, falling 36 francs to 2,279. Roche fell 370 francs to 13,770.
Swiss Life, which jumped 12 percent on Tuesday, rose 64 francs to 985. Dealers speculated that Swiss banks may be buying the stock.

On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex) a total of 178,379 options were traded. Dealers said that trading in UBS calls alone accounted for 61,000 of the volume. On the futures side, 16,703 SMI futures changed hands. About half of them were August futures, which ended down 140 points at 5,670.
